topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe conventional therapeutic modalities and the physiological challenges, systemic toxicities, and drug-efflux mechanisms that limit their effectiveness.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific vulnerabilities, such as hormone dependence, checkpoint failure, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted therapy against driving oncogenic kinases, exploring inhibitor mechanisms, clinical resistance pathways, and adaptive dosing strategies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the engineering and application of monoclonal antibodies to neutralize surface receptors and selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapeutic interventions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the immune system's role in cancer defense and the clinical implementation of immunotherapies that reactivate or engineer T cells against tumors.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical mortality trends, current clinical hurdles, and emerging paradigms shaping the future of cancer treatment and prevention.
